hook: A tiny silver bell, and an extremely polite butler who shows up whenever someone rings it. Most of the file reads like a comedy of manners, a running tally of what he will and won't do. Watch how the article builds your expectations, because it is not quite as cosy as it first appears.
whyItMatters: SCP-662 is a classic of the useful-anomaly type: an object the Foundation treats less as a threat than as a tool it is a little too pleased to own. It also shows how much personality an early-numbered entry can draw from a simple list format, with the butler's courtesy and his limits doing nearly all the characterisation.
thingsToNotice:
The addendum is the heart of the piece. Its rhythm of request and result, often a polite refusal, sets up jokes about board games and one doctor who keeps abusing the privilege, then slips a couple of far darker entries into the same cheerful register. That tonal whiplash is deliberate: the bell grants things without weighing the character of whoever rings it, within whatever rules the butler privately keeps.

Notice also the out-of-sight rule. Nobody ever catches him arriving or leaving, and the acquisition story makes clear that the bell, not the man, is what binds him, while the engraving inside hints at a previous owner the file never explains.

related.note: Another ask-for-anything object whose limits are half the fun.
Another item the Foundation keeps feeding odd requests just to map its rules.
